$meta.role: Design -> code map for @sayva/design-system. Every design token and contracted primitive is either implemented, or explicitly deferred/blocked with a reason. An entry with neither fails CI from Slice 3 onward.
$meta.scopeDecision: D1 - Phase 1 implements the token layer, the 10 Design System primitives and one shared overlay substrate hook. The 12 Design System patterns are out of scope; see outOfScope.patterns. The design's own phase1 flag marks 17 components, 7 of which are patterns this decision defers.

statusVocabulary.deferred: In Phase 1 scope, not yet implemented.
statusVocabulary.implemented-pending-signoff: Emitted from a recorded decision because the design states the value in prose but carries no token. Awaiting design-owner sign-off; reported by the token tests until it arrives.
statusVocabulary.blocked: Cannot be implemented without a design decision. Carries a reason naming the open decision.
statusVocabulary.implemented: Present in code and covered by the parity test.
statusVocabulary.out-of-scope: Deliberately not in Phase 1. Carries a reason.

$meta.codeField: The custom properties a design token produced. An array because the mapping is not always 1:1 — a typography token expands to three, a resizable pane range to two, and a blocked token to none.

tokens.reason: D9 — the stated value `cubic(.2,0,0,1)` is not a CSS function. Expanding it to cubic-bezier() preserves all four control points but is an interpretation of a malformed value, so it awaits confirmation. Pending open decision D9.
D9 — as ease.standard, for `cubic(.4,0,1,1)`. Pending open decision D9.
C1 / D4 — Foundations §15 states 28px, the Design System density prop states 26px. Both canonical; the design owner must pick. Pending open decision D4.

tokens.expansion: A resizable range, so both ends are emitted. Collapsing them to one number would mean choosing a default the design never gave.
A resizable range, so both ends are emitted, as pane.sidebar.
Not a min-width. §10.9 defines bp.sm as "< 900px", the base range below --breakpoint-md; it has no threshold of its own to emit.

tokens.reason: F9 / D5 — UNSPECIFIED BY DESIGN as a token. §16 states the rule in prose ("a 2px accent ring with a 2px offset, never removed") but the design carries no focus.ring.{color,width,offset} trio. D5 is open and pending the design owner: neither adopted nor rejected. Meanwhile base.css implements the rule from --color-accent-default, with the two 2px figures as literals copied verbatim from §16.

components.note: Variant `icon-only` requires `label` at the TypeScript level, and `disabled` requires `disabledReason`, so neither can be omitted at runtime. The primary variant's label uses surface.default as its foreground: the design has no token for a figure on a filled ground, and that is the value the canonical screen draws. Recorded as open decision D12.

Eight variants x nine states, all in one slice. Three states are observed rather than set: `empty` and `filled` follow the value and `focus` is :focus-visible, which base.css owns. `readonly` and `disabled` each require a reason at the TypeScript level, per the canonical specimen's "Reason shown, never silently disabled" - a rule neither the handoff nor the inventory records. `suggested` renders the AI register (accent.ai.*); its accept and reject affordances belong to SySuggestion, which wraps this field and is out of Phase 1 scope. Invalid is border + icon + text, the icon being the Unicode character the specimen draws, so no icon set is involved and D6 is untouched.
components.contractNote: The plan split SyField across two slices on the assumption that combobox needed the overlay substrate. It does not: in the ARIA combobox pattern focus stays in the input and a virtual cursor moves via aria-activedescendant, so there is nothing to trap, stack or restore. All eight variants therefore landed together. `sizes` is UNSPECIFIED BY DESIGN and none were invented. "⌘S saves the form" is listed in the contract's keyboard row but is form-scoped, not field-scoped, and is not implemented here.

components.note: Five tones x two placements. Decision D3: the canonical contract lists this component's states as the six editorial lifecycle values, which must not enter the design system. The component exposes `tone`, named after the five status token families, and apps/studio owns the lifecycle -> (glyph, tone, label) mapping. Each tone renders a complete status triplet (AC15). The design records no sizes (UNSPECIFIED BY DESIGN).

Five states x four variants. Decision D3: `typeLabel` is a plain string, not a union of entity types — the component is "a pointer to any entity" and which entities exist is the application's business. The `deprecated` state requires `replacement`, nullable, because SS15.3 allows "replacement declared or explicitly none" but never silence. Deleted references render struck through with a visible note, per the canonical specimen's "unresolvable refs render struck through with a 'deleted' note - never a blank", which the handoff and inventory both omit.
components.contractNote: Variant values are named chip / row / inline / thumbnail; the inventory records them as "inline text" and "with thumbnail (assets)". The recorded names are prose labels for the same four variants. Coverage is asserted against `states`, where the names match once the explanatory gloss is stripped.

components.note: Six states x three sizes. `denominator` is required and forms part of the accessible name, per SS13.7's "78% alone is a rumour". The optional bar is aria-hidden decoration drawn from the viz.* ramp; AC16 is satisfied by construction rather than by lint, since a bar can only appear alongside the required `figure`. Becomes a button when `onOpen` is given, per P10 "every metric is a door".

Six absence states x three sizes. `error` requires a traceId and an action at the TypeScript level, because AC14 fails an error without a trace ID and a retry; `loading` is a skeleton with a label rather than a heading, per the contract's "Skeleton, not spinner". Errors announce assertively (role=alert), every other state politely (role=status) — the contract names only errors and empties, so the rest take the polite default. No illustration or icon slot exists: "no decorative illustration", and the icon set is open decision D6.
components.contractNote: The inventory's `variants` field repeats the three sizes rather than listing the six absence states; the handoff's §11 row and this entry's `states` field carry the six. Left verbatim as ingested — coverage is asserted against `states` and `sizes`.

components.substrate: src/overlay — the shared overlay substrate the design contracts as "a hook, not a component". Provides Esc-closes-topmost, focus restoration to the trigger (A07) and a stack capped at depth two (A07, §15.9). Containment is an opt-in flag on it, per D14.
components.note: role="menu" per decision D15, which the design states outright in this component's own accessibility cell. Non-modal per decision D14: Tab is not contained — it moves focus onward and the menu closes behind it. The eight fixed groups the contract names — Open, Edit, Relate, Lifecycle, Validate, Duplicate, Copy link, Destructive (last) — are the entity action registry's vocabulary and stay in apps/studio under decision D3, exactly as SyStatusBadge's lifecycle values do. This component renders the groups it is handed in the order it is handed them, so "destructive items last" remains the registry's guarantee rather than a reordering performed behind the caller's back. Item tone is presentational, and the destructive group is set apart structurally by a separator as well as by colour (P5). Unpermitted items require their reason at the TypeScript level and tie it to the item with aria-describedby. Width is content-driven: sizes are UNSPECIFIED BY DESIGN and none was invented.

Decision D14 rules this surface non-modal: it shares the overlay substrate but does not contain Tab. Decision D16 governs `resizing` — the state is explicitly SyDrawer's own in the design, but nothing dimensional supports it (§10.8's sizing table has rows for the rail, sidebar and inspector and none for a drawer), so when this is built the state will be declared and inert, marked blocked citing D16, with no resize affordance and no invented width.

states: stale (computed by an older model version)
components.note: Five states x three variants. The design records no sizes for this component (UNSPECIFIED BY DESIGN), so none were invented. The numeric value always leads and is always in the accessible name (AI RULE 3); the bar is decoration and takes one fill rather than encoding the band in colour, because the band is a word.
